items.title: After a Positive Noninvasive Colorectal Screening Result, What Happens Next Matters: Geneoscopy Launches ColoSense NextStep
items.content:
After a Positive Noninvasive Colorectal Screening Result, What Happens Next Matters: Geneoscopy Launches ColoSense NextStep - Geneoscopy - Transforming Gastrointestinal Health About Us Our Leadership Advisors Our Lab & Our Credentials Corporate Responsibility Contact Us Gastrointestinal Health Colorectal Cancer Screening Inflammatory Bowel Disease Other Gastrointestinal Diseases Clinical Evidence Partnerships BioPharma Partnerships Research Partnerships Newsroom Press Releases News & Stories Videos & Podcasts Media Inquiries Join Our Team Search After a Positive Noninvasive Colorectal Screening Result, What Happens Next Matters: Geneoscopy Launches ColoSense NextStep October 20, 2026 | In Press Release | By Geneoscopy After a Positive Noninvasive Colorectal Screening Result, What Happens Next Matters: Geneoscopy Launches ColoSense NextStep New provider-enabled navigation program gives patients live, personalized support after a positive ColoSense result — addressing barriers to follow-up colonoscopy needed to complete screening ST. LOUIS (Tuesday, October 20, 2026) — Geneoscopy, Inc., a healthcare diagnostics company advancing the next generation of tools for gastrointestinal health, today announced the launch of ColoSense NextStep , a provider-enabled, opt-in patient navigation program designed to help patients with a positive ColoSense colorectal cancer (CRC) screening test result move toward the recommended follow-up colonoscopy to complete screening. Too many patients do not take that critical next step. In a study of nearly 33,000 people with a positive stool-based screening result, only 56 percent received a follow-up colonoscopy within one year.¹ Incomplete follow-up can have serious consequences. Research has found that failure to complete follow-up colonoscopy after a positive stool-based screening test is associated with twice the risk of death from colorectal cancer.² ColoSense NextStep addresses this critical gap For providers who opt in, the program helps patients understand why follow-up matters, address practical barriers, and move toward the recommended follow-up colonoscopy to complete CRC screening. The program’s goal is to help patients complete follow-up colonoscopy within 90 days of a positive ColoSense result. Geneoscopy developed ColoSense, its FDA-approved, RNA-based CRC screening test, as an at-home option for average-risk adults 45 and older. With ColoSense NextStep, the company is extending its support beyond test completion and result communication to help patients take the critical next step after a positive result. “A positive screening result can be an overwhelming moment for patients,” said Erica Barnell, MD, PhD, cofounder and chief science and medical officer of Geneoscopy. “Some patients have questions about what the result means, what happens next, and how to arrange follow-up care. ColoSense NextStep is designed to provide personal support at that critical moment – so patients don’t have to navigate the path to colonoscopy alone.” Noninvasive screening can expand access, but its full benefit depends on what happens after a positive result. By addressing common practical barriers to follow-up, ColoSense NextStep is designed to help participating providers, health systems, and payers support patients in completing the full CRC screening process when they need additional care. Live support when it matters most For providers who enroll in ColoSense NextStep, their patients will receive consented outreach by text, email, or phone. The NextStep Clinical Support Team provides general education on the importance of follow-up colonoscopy and what patients can expect, answers general questions about the next step in care, and helps patients identify practical barriers that could delay follow-up. When requested, the team may also share publicly available, non-directive information about nearby or in-network gastroenterology providers and general transportation or access-to-care resources. Patients who need additional assistance can access live support. “For providers, health systems, and payers, initial test completion is only one measure of an effective colorectal cancer screening program,” said Andrew Barnell, co-founder and chief executive officer of Geneoscopy. “For patients with a positive noninvasive result, timely follow-up colonoscopy is necessary to complete screening and realize its full benefit. ColoSense NextStep gives providers an additional resource to help address barriers to follow-up – supporting a more complete, patient-centered approach to colorectal cancer screening.” ColoSense NextStep reflects Geneoscopy’s commitment to the full colorectal cancer screening process by helping patients move from a positive result toward appropriate diagnostic follow-up, while giving participating providers an additional resource to support care when it matters most. To learn more about ColoSense NextStep, visit colosense.com/colosense-nextstep ### About ColoSense NextStep ColoSense NextStep is Geneoscopy’s provider-enabled, opt-in patient navigation program for patients with a positive (abnormal) ColoSense result. The program provides educational and communication support related to follow-up colonoscopy after a positive ColoSense result. Participation is voluntary and subject to applicable provider opt-in, patient consent, privacy, and communication requirements. The cost of NextStep is included with each order as part of the standard ColoSense patient experience. ColoSense NextStep is not a healthcare provider. It does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment recommendations; schedule procedures, make referrals, or guarantee colonoscopy completion or clinical outcomes. NextStep does not pay for medical care, cover transportation or other related expenses. The patient and the patient’s healthcare provider remain responsible for all clinical decisions. About ColoSense ColoSense is Geneoscopy’s FDA-approved, multi-target stool RNA test for the qualitative detection of colorectal neoplasia-associated RNA markers and occult hemoglobin in human stool. Geneoscopy developed ColoSense as a noninvasive CRC screening option for average-risk adults 45 and older. ColoSense is listed as a preferred screening option in the American Cancer Society colorectal cancer screening guidelines and included in the National Comprehensive Cancer Network (NCCN) guidelines. A positive ColoSense result should be followed by appropriate diagnostic evaluation, including colonoscopy, as determined by a healthcare provider. ColoSense is not a replacement for diagnostic or surveillance colonoscopy in high-risk individuals. ColoSense is available nationwide through Geneoscopy’s commercial collaboration with Labcorp, enabling broad access for providers and patients through its nationwide network. For more information, visit colosense.com. About Geneoscopy Geneoscopy is a healthcare diagnostics company focused on advancing gastrointestinal health by designing tools for real-world care. The company’s proprietary, patented RNA-based biomarker platform powers its FDA-approved ColoSense test for CRC screening and supports continued development of clinically useful diagnostic tools for gastrointestinal health. For more information, visit geneoscopy.com. MEDIA CONTACT media@geneoscopy.com INVESTOR RELATIONS CONTACT Amit Bhalla, Chief Financial Officer amit.bhalla@geneoscopy.com     ¹ Mohl JT, et al. stories.title: 燃石医学与Myriad达成全球技术授权战略合作，携手拓展新一代HRD检测全球版图

rationales.relevance: 事件涉及燃石医学（Burning Rock）的HRD检测产品拓展及全球战略合作。虽然HRD检测主要属于伴随诊断（CDx）和精准治疗领域，而非直接的多癌种早期筛查（MCED），但燃石医学是癌症早筛领域的关键竞争者，且其业务涵盖“基于液体活检的多癌种早检”。该合作强化了其在肿瘤基因检测平台（OncoScreen Plus）上的技术积累和全球商业化能力，对理解其整体竞争态势有直接参考价值，故评为癌症筛查直接相关（外围核心）。
rationales.impact: 这是一项实质性的商业和技术进展。燃石医学通过与Myriad Genetics深化合作，获得了新一代HRD算法的全球授权（除特定地区外），并计划将其整合到自主研发的OncoScreen Plus平台上。这不仅扩展了现有产品线（新增前列腺癌prGIS模块），还标志着其从中国市场向全球多个核心市场的商业化扩张。对于竞品档案而言，这反映了燃石在伴随诊断领域的技术壁垒构建和国际化布局的重要变化。
rationales.actionability: 需要持续跟踪。虽然该事件不直接改变早筛产品的临床格局，但需关注OncoScreen Plus平台后续是否会将此类多组学/基因组分析能力复用到早筛产品中，以及其全球商业化策略对早筛市场准入的影响。目前无需立即响应，但应更新竞品档案中的技术平台和全球战略部分。

达成全新的全球技术授权战略合作。双方将进一步深化在HRD（同源重组缺陷）检测领域的战略合作，共同推动myChoice HRD Plus产品技术拓展，并基于燃石医学自主研发的OncoScreen Plus平台搭载全新授权技术，开发新一代HRD检测试剂盒，商业化领域从中国扩大到全球多个核心市场。 燃石医学与Myriad的合作可追溯至2020年，彼时双方首次官宣达成独家技术授权战略合作，将Myriad获得FDA批准的HRD基因组不稳定性评分（Genomic Instability Score, GIS）算法引入中国进行市场开发和商业化。2021年，燃石医学依托该技术完成多维度性能验证，正式推出myChoice HRD Plus产品，为国内患者提供精准可靠的HRD检测服务，助力临床医生识别可能从PARP抑制剂治疗中获益的肿瘤人群。 依托全新的战略合作，myChoice HRD Plus即将进一步扩展检测能力，在保留原有HRD基因组不稳定性评分（GIS）检测基础上新增针对前列腺癌的基因组不稳定性评分（prostate Genomic Instability Score, prGIS）算法模块。该算法通过综合评估基因组层面的端粒等位基因失衡（Telomeric Allelic Imbalance, TAI）、大片段迁移（Large-scale State Transitions, LST）及全基因组不平衡（Genome Wide Imbalance, GWI）等基因组瘢痕特征，精准评估前列腺癌患者的HRD状态，为临床开展个体化治疗决策提供重要依据。新的myChoice HRD Plus将进一步拓展HRD检测在前列腺癌精准诊疗中的应用价值。燃石医学将持续致力于该产品在中国的开发和商业化，推动全球领先的HRD检测技术惠及更多国内患者。 与此同时，燃石医学将结合Myriad全球授权的GIS算法（日本除外）和prGIS算法（日本和美国除外）及丰富的产品开发经验，在自主研发的OncoScreen Plus平台上开发新一代HRD检测试剂盒，强化燃石医学"One Assay for All"的全球战略布局。该产品将进一步提升HRD状态评估的精准性和可及性，为全球肿瘤患者提供更加权威、高效的精准诊断支持。 未来，新的myChoice HRD Plus及基于OncoScreen Plus开发的新一代HRD检测试剂盒将为全球药企合作伙伴提供更加高效、灵活的伴随诊断（CDx）解决方案，赋能创新药物研发及商业化推广，也能让更多肿瘤患者获得基于分子分型指导的个性化精准治疗方案。 关于燃石医学 燃石医学（纳斯达克代码：BNR）成立于2014年，公司使命为"用科学守护生命之光"，专注于开发创新可靠、具有临床价值的癌症伴随诊断与早检产品。公司业务及研发方向主要覆盖：1）癌症患病人群精准医学检测；2）全球抗肿瘤药企的生物标志物和伴随诊断合作；3）基于液体活检的多癌种早检。燃石医学于2018年7月获国家药品监督管理局（NMPA）颁发的中国肿瘤NGS检测试剂盒第一证，在体外诊断领域具有里程碑式意义。实验室获得广东省临检中心颁发的 "高通量测序实验室"技术审核，同时获得美国CLIA、CAP和ISO15189实验室质量体系资质认证。公司将继续致力于开发创新可靠的癌症精准检测产品，推动癌症精准医疗领域的发展。 About Myriad Genetics Myriad Genetics is a leading molecular diagnostic and precision medicine company committed to advancing health and well-being for all. Myriad Genetics develops and commercializes molecular tests that help patients and providers uncover genetic insights. Our tests assess the risk of developing disease or disease progression and guide treatment decisions across medical specialties where molecular insights can significantly improve patient care, support earlier detection, enable more precise treatment and contribute to lowering healthcare costs. # Geneseeq Canada Named First Genomic Testing Partner in UHN’s SHERLOCK Study

July 14, 2026

\|In [Homepage](https://na.geneseeq.com/category/homepage/ "View all posts in Homepage")

\|By [Geneseeq](https://na.geneseeq.com/author/rebakah/)

_Collaboration supports genomic profiling and molecular monitoring research within one of Canada’s largest prospective cancer genomics and molecular residual disease studies_

**TORONTO, Canada –**\[July 14th,2026\] – Geneseeq Technology Inc. (Geneseeq Canada) is pleased to announce its support of cancer research initiatives at University Health Network (UHN), Canada’s leading research hospital, which includes Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, recognized as one of the world’s top 10 cancer centres (Newsweek).  One of the major initiatives included in this collaboration is the [SHERLOCK study](https://www.uhn.ca/sherlock) (ClinicalTrials.gov [NCT07524114](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07524114)), a large-scale prospective cancer research platform at UHN’s Princess Margaret Cancer Centre.

Through its collaboration with UHN investigators, Geneseeq Canada is providing genomic testing, molecular residual disease (MRD) monitoring capabilities, and support for precision oncology translational research in Canada, including genomic testing and molecular monitoring services for approximately 1,000 patients participating in the SHERLOCK study.

The study is expected to enroll approximately 7,000 patients over five years across multiple solid tumours and hematologic malignancies. By following patients over time and analyzing tumour tissue and blood samples, SHERLOCK aims to better understand treatment response, disease recurrence, and cancer evolution, while evaluating how genomic technologies may help inform future cancer care.

For selected participants enrolled in the SHERLOCK program, Geneseeq technologies may be used for specific genomic profiling and molecular monitoring activities, where applicable and depending on study needs and sample availability. For participants with solid tumours, baseline tumour tissue samples may be analyzed using [GeneseeqPrime®](https://na.geneseeq.com/geneseeqprime/), Geneseeq’s comprehensive genomic profiling assay, to characterize the molecular features of their cancers. Longitudinal blood samples may be analyzed using [Shielding® Ultra](https://na.geneseeq.com/minimal-residual-disease/), Geneseeq’s molecular monitoring technology designed to track cancer-related signals with high sensitivity over time using either matched tumour tissue information or blood samples alone. For participants with hematologic malignancies, genomic analyses may be performed using [Hemasalus®,](https://na.geneseeq.com/pan-cancer-panels-for-hematologic-malignancies/#hemasalus_test) Geneseeq’s comprehensive genomic profiling assay for blood cancers.

_“Canada has played an important role in Geneseeq’s journey,”_ said **Dr. Xue Wu, CEO of Geneseeq Canada.** _“We are pleased to support Canadian-led cancer research through the SHERLOCK program and honoured to become its first commercial genomic testing partner. Our participation reflects Geneseeq’s long-term commitment to advancing the scientific understanding of cancer genomics and MRD while supporting research that may ultimately benefit patients.”_

_“Advancing precision oncology requires close collaboration between academic institutions, healthcare systems, and industry partners,”_ said **Dr. Lillian Siu, Clinician and Senior Scientist at UHN’s Princess Margaret Cancer Centre.** _“One of the biggest challenges in cancer care is knowing whether curative treatment has truly eliminated cancer or whether the disease remains and may return._ Through SHERLOCK, we are following patients over time and combining genomic analyses with clinical outcomes to better understand treatment response, detect signs of recurrence earlier, and generate evidence that could help guide future approaches to cancer monitoring and care.”

SHERLOCK is expected to generate important evidence regarding the biological and clinical significance of molecular residual disease and may help inform future precision oncology strategies, clinical trial design, and biomarker research. It is also one of several ongoing collaborative efforts between Geneseeq and UHN investigators aimed at advancing cancer genomics, early detection, molecular residual disease research, and precision oncology.

**[About Geneseeq](https://na.geneseeq.com/)**

Geneseeq Technology Inc. is the Canadian subsidiary of Geneseeq, a global precision oncology company advancing cancer detection, diagnosis, and treatment through next-generation sequencing (NGS) technologies. Headquartered in Ontario, Canada, the company operates CAP- and CLIA-certified laboratory that supports cancer genomic research, precision oncology programs and global clinical collaborations.

As part of the global Geneseeq organization, Geneseeq Technology Inc. provides access to an integrated portfolio spanning comprehensive genomic profiling across tumour types, minimal residual disease (MRD) monitoring, and multi-cancer early detection (MCED) solutions. Its flagship comprehensive genomic profiling assay, GeneseeqPrime®, is FDA-cleared in the United States, CE-IVD marked in Europe, and NMPA-approved in China. The company’s Shielding® Ultra MRD assay and Hemasalus® hematological malignancy genomic profiling assay are also CE-IVD marked.

Together with the broader Geneseeq organization, Geneseeq Technology Inc. collaborates with hospitals, academic institutions, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide to support precision medicine, translational research, and biomarker-driven therapeutic development.

       今日，基准医疗宣布与帝基生物（DiaCarta）——一家专注精准分子诊断和新型肿瘤、传染病检测产品开发的公司，达成长期合作关系， **双方将在癌症筛查产品开发和全球商业化方面进行合作。**

       基准医疗和帝基生物在此次合作中将利用各自在DNA甲基化和突变检测方面的专有技术，面向全球市场，共同开发分子诊断产品并致力实现快速的商业转化。

基准医疗的DNA甲基化检测诊断产品UriFind曾于2021年7月获美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）“突破性医疗器械”认定。目前，基准医疗正在美国开展一项前瞻性注册临床试验 (NCT05643690)，用于UriFind产品的PMA申请（ [https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05643690)， 帝基生物也作为临床检验实验室之一参与其中。](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05643690)%EF%BC%8C%E5%B8%9D%E5%9F%BA%E7%94%9F%E7%89%A9%E4%B9%9F%E4%BD%9C%E4%B8%BA%E4%B8%B4%E5%BA%8A%E6%A3%80%E9%AA%8C%E5%AE%9E%E9%AA%8C%E5%AE%A4%E4%B9%8B%E4%B8%80%E5%8F%82%E4%B8%8E%E5%85%B6%E4%B8%AD%E3%80%82)

**帝基生物首席执行官兼总裁张爱国博士表示：**“此次与基准医疗的合作，能够结合两家公司的技术专长，使我们在开发高精度突变和甲基化检测诊断产品时得以实现高灵敏度和高特异性，从而满足不断发展的精确诊断的需求。”

**基准医疗创始人兼首席执行官范建兵博士表示：**“我们一直致力于将最好的癌症诊断产品推向全球市场。此次与帝基生物达成合作，将加速基准医疗现有癌症筛查产品的海外商业化，并在未来共同开发出更多新的产品。”

随着癌症成为中国乃至全球的主要重大疾病，癌症早期检测和诊断需要一个全球性的战略和解决方案。通过与帝基生物的合作，基准医疗希望加速其早期癌症筛查全球计划，并开发一条强大的产品线。

关于 DiaCarta

帝基生物（DiaCarta）是一家全球领先的分子诊断公司，致力于开发创新技术，并通过使用液体活检提供有效的精确诊断，改变患者护理。除了 FDA EUA 批准的 QuantiVirus™ SARS-CoV-2 检测外，DiaCarta 还提供一系列检测服务，从 QClamp® qPCR 检测到 OptiSeq™ XNA-NGS 面板。其新颖的 XNA 技术，通过相对降低野生型序列并富集突变目标序列，从而提高产品的灵敏度；利用这项技术，公司开发了高灵敏度的结肠直肠癌血液早期检测 ColoScape™。凭借其 isobDNA™ 技术 - 该技术通过放大信号提供高水平的检测，无需 RNA/DNA 提取或扩增 - 公司开发了革命性的 RadTox™ 测试，用于个性化放疗和化疗，评估肿瘤反应并加强患者护理。公司位于加利福尼亚州普莱森顿，是 ISO 认证的 GMP 合规公司，并为客户提供 CLIA 认证的实验室服务。

stories.title: 基准医疗SABCS首发：ctDNA甲基化与乳腺超声联合早诊模型可降低不必要的活检/手术率

rationales.relevance: 该事件涉及基准医疗在乳腺癌早诊领域的ctDNA甲基化联合超声模型研究，属于癌症筛查直接相关领域。虽然主要聚焦于单癌种（乳腺癌）的辅助诊断以减少过度诊疗，而非多癌种早期检测（MCED），但其技术路径（液体活检+影像）与世和基因等公司的多癌种筛查产品存在潜在的技术交叉和市场关联，故评为20分。
rationales.impact: 这是一项实质性的临床进展披露。SABCS壁报展示及具体数据（准确性提升40.58%，不必要活检率降低43.47%）表明该公司在特定场景下解决了临床痛点（BI-RADS 4a类结节的过度诊疗）。这值得纳入竞品档案，作为其技术能力和差异化定位的证据，但尚未达到改变整体竞争格局或获得重大监管批准的里程碑级别。
rationales.actionability: 需要持续跟踪。目前仅为会议壁报形式的初步学术披露，需关注后续是否有更大规模的前瞻性临床试验、注册申报进展或商业化落地情况，以评估其对世和基因现有产品线或未来布局的实际威胁或合作机会。暂无立即响应的紧迫性。

items.content:
![f2_banpc-549.jpg](https://www.anchordx.com/Public/Uploads/uploadfile/images/20220726/f2_banpc-549.jpg)![f2_banph-115.jpg](https://www.anchordx.com/Public/Uploads/uploadfile/images/20220726/f2_banph-115.jpg)

# 基准医疗SABCS首发：ctDNA甲基化与乳腺超声联合早诊模型可降低不必要的活检/手术率

![](https://www.anchordx.com/Public/Cn/images/icon-clock.svg)2023-02-09

- [![](https://www.anchordx.com/Public/Cn/images/icon-home.svg)](https://www.anchordx.com/)
- [新闻动态](https://www.anchordx.com/news/activity)
- [学术交流](https://www.anchordx.com/news/communication)

![](https://www.anchordx.com/Public/ueditor/upload/image/20230209/1675931718752860.gif)

![](https://www.anchordx.com/Public/ueditor/upload/image/20230209/1675931719875208.png)

圣安东尼奥乳腺癌研讨会（San Antonio Breast Cancer Symposium，SABCS）于2022年 12 月 6 日至 10 日举行，**基准医疗与哈尔滨医科大学附属肿瘤医院庞达教授团队联合发表的学术研究——《乳腺超声与ctDNA甲基化联合模型可提高乳腺癌早期诊断性能》（Improving the Performance of Breast Cancer Early Diagnosis by a Model Combining Breast Ultrasound with Methylation Markers in Plasma Circulating Tumor DNA），**被本次大会以壁报形式收录，并在会议现场进行了展示和交流。

基准医疗研发团队经过数年的探索发现：**ctDNA甲基化检测在乳腺结节良恶性鉴别方面表现优越，有挑战传统影像学的趋势，有望弥补乳腺超声诊断的不足，减少不必要的穿刺和手术，避免过度诊疗。****1**

**减少BI-RADS 4a不必要的活检/手术，避免过度诊疗**

与乳腺超声相比，**“乳腺癌特异的ctDNA甲基化-超声联合模型”**对BI-RADS 4a类患者的**准确性提高了40.58%**，不必要的**活检/手术率降低了43.47%**。也就是说，如果此技术可应用于乳腺癌早诊，近一半的BI-RADS 4a类患者可**避免接受有创的乳房活检/手术。**

**2**

**区分导管原位癌和浸润性导管癌，避免过度手术****“乳腺癌特异的ctDNA甲基化模型”**对良性乳腺病变，导管原位癌 (DCIS) 和浸润性导管癌 (IDC)的恶性概率预测随着恶性程度和浸润程度的加深而递增，有**进一步区分导管内癌（DCIS）和浸润性导管癌（IDC）的潜力，从而减少不必要的手术和过度治疗。****3**

**更符合中国人群特征的早诊技术，助力“两癌”筛查**早在2021年，基准医疗就在Nature子刊《npj Breast Cancer》（中科院一区）发表了题为《外周血游离DNA甲基化模型用于乳腺癌诊断》（Circulating cell-free DNA-based methylation patterns for breastcancer diagnosis）的文章 [（原文请点击）](http://mp.weixin.qq.com/s?__biz=MzIzMjA5NDM1NQ==&mid=2653540462&idx=1&sn=b6725632abf4477cd602a2d28d40b336&chksm=f3475f92c430d68482d8380b769bbae6d7dd5261cc2482ef9e43903eb9d85293bd093b48176f&scene=21#wechat_redirect)，首次证明外周血游离DNA甲基化检测在乳腺癌诊断方面的效果堪比、甚至超过乳腺钼靶。作为国内首家深入研究ctDNA甲基化检测在乳腺癌早诊的公司，此项研究为基准医疗在**符合中国人特征的筛查方式（乳腺超声）上，对乳腺癌早期精准诊断所做的进一步探索。**基准医疗力求早日完成乳腺癌早诊产品的开发，造福广大女性群体。

**乳腺癌筛查现状**

目前乳腺癌已经成为严重威胁女性健康最常见的恶性肿瘤。大量循证医学证据表明，**乳腺癌筛查可以提高乳腺癌早期诊断率、降低病死率。**近10余年来，随着中国乳腺癌科普和宣教工作的开展，以及国家卫健委 **“两癌筛查（宫颈癌和乳腺癌）”** 工作的进行，女性乳腺癌防癌意识逐渐增强，参与乳腺癌早期筛查的女性比例逐年提高，乳腺癌早诊率也在逐年提高\[1\]。但是，早诊率的提高也加大了乳腺结节患者过度诊疗。当乳腺结节被判定为**BI-RAD4aS 级时**（纤维腺瘤、有乳头溢液或溢血的导管内病灶及不能明确的乳腺炎症等）：指南规定“可进一步影像学检查，必要时活检”\[2\]；但是根据市场调研结果，**90%的4a级患者会行进一步穿刺活检或者微创手术。**临床证据表明4a结节患者**恶性率** **仅为2%~10%**，因此导致大量不必要的过度活检或手术。本研究有望减少不必要的穿刺和手术。

**DCIS和IDC区分的意义**

在WHO乳腺肿瘤分类中，已将导管原位癌（DCIS）列入癌前病变，不属于真正意义上的癌；因此，关于DCIS是否需要被诊断以及是否存在过度治疗一直有争议。治疗方式上，DCIS可以选择保留乳房的手术和全乳放疗，不涉及化疗；而浸润性导管癌（IDC）的治疗方法主要有手术切除和放化疗\[3\]。本研究可避免DCIS的过度治疗。

**关于SABCS**

此届SABCS会议有来自 80 多个国家的 8,000 名国际学术、研究人员和医生参与。该研讨会提供有关乳腺癌和癌前乳腺疾病的实验生物学，病因学，预防，诊断和治疗的最新信息，旨在实现临床转化和基础研究的平衡，为研究人员、卫生专业人员以及对乳腺癌特别感兴趣的人提供互动、沟通和教育的平台。

**参考文献**

\[1\]中国研究型医院学会乳腺专业委员会中国女性乳腺癌筛查指南制定专家组. 中国女性乳腺癌筛查指南(2022年版)\[J\]. 中国研究型医院, 2022, 9(2):8.

\[2\]沈洪兵, 田金徽, 周宝森. 中国女性乳腺癌筛查与早诊早治指南(2021,北京)\[J\]. 中国肿瘤, 2021, 30(3):31.

\[3\]包凌云. 乳腺导管原位癌的超声诊断\[J\]. 浙江医学, 2019, 41(11):5.

items.content:
[Skip to content](https://grail.com/press-releases/grail-to-present-at-the-ubs-global-healthcare-conference/#content)

October 27, 2026

SUNNYVALE, Calif., Oct. 27, 2026 — GRAIL, Inc. (Nasdaq: GRAL), a healthcare company whose mission is to detect cancer early when it can be cured, today announced that company management will present at the UBS Global Healthcare Conference in Palm Beach, FL on Tuesday, Nov. 10 at 11:00 a.m. ET.

A live and replay webcast may be accessed in the investor relations section of GRAIL’s website at [investors.grail.com](http://investors.grail.com/). The webcast will be archived and available for reply for at least 30 days after the event.

**About GRAIL**

GRAIL is a healthcare company whose mission is to detect cancer early, when it can be cured. GRAIL is focused on alleviating the global burden of cancer by using the power of next-generation sequencing, population-scale clinical studies, and state-of-the-art machine learning, software, and automation to detect and identify multiple deadly cancer types in earlier stages. GRAIL’s targeted methylation-based platform can support the continuum of care for screening and precision oncology, including multi-cancer early detection in symptomatic patients, risk stratification, minimal residual disease detection, biomarker subtyping, treatment and recurrence monitoring. GRAIL is headquartered in Sunnyvale, Calif. with locations in Washington, D.C., North Carolina, and the United Kingdom.

For more information, visit [grail.com](http://grail.com/).

ESMO Congress 2026: Gene Solutions to Present AI-Enabled Multi-omic Liquid Biopsy - Advancing Healthcare Through AI-powered Genetic Testing Skip to content OUR SOLUTIONS triSure SPOT-MAS K-TRACK | K-4CARE ​ ABOUT US Our Vision Our Laboratories​ Leadership Team Contact us​ OUR SCIENCE Publications & Abstracts NEWS & INSIGHTS OUR SOLUTIONS triSure SPOT-MAS K-TRACK | K-4CARE ​ ABOUT US Our Vision Our Laboratories​ Leadership Team Contact us​ OUR SCIENCE Publications & Abstracts NEWS & INSIGHTS ESMO Congress 2026: Gene Solutions to Present AI-Enabled Multi-omic Liquid Biopsy September 22, 2026 News Gene Solutions will host an Industry Satellite Symposium at ESMO Congress 2026, bringing together international experts to examine how AI-enabled multi-omics and cell-free DNA analysis can move from technological innovation to evidence-based decisions that health systems can implement at scale across the cancer care continuum. ESMO Congress 2026 will take place 23–27 October in Madrid. The session is scheduled for Friday, 23 October, 09:45–11:15 CEST , in the Salamanca Auditorium, Hall 10, IFEMA Madrid. AI and multi-omics are opening new possibilities across cancer detection, treatment selection, and disease monitoring. The question now is how the growing evidence can support accessible testing and decisions that health systems can implement at scale. AI-Enabled Multi-omic Liquid Biopsy Across the Cancer Care Continuum: From Technological Innovation to Scalable Clinical Implementation The programme addresses a practical gap in precision oncology: how multi-omic liquid biopsy can be applied across the cancer care continuum—from earlier detection through high-precision treatment applications—with the evidence, affordability, and implementation pathways that clinical practice requires. Examining the next generation of multi-cancer early detection Opening the scientific programme, Prof. Umberto Malapelle of the University of Naples Federico II will examine the clinical challenges associated with current multi-cancer early detection tests. The presentation, “Clinical Challenges with Multi-Cancer Early Detection Tests: Unmet Needs and Lessons for Next-Generation Approaches in Precision Oncology,” will address the clinical questions and evidence requirements that will shape the next generation of early cancer detection approaches. Combining AI, multi-omics, and cell-free DNA analysis Dr. Le Son Tran of the Medical Genetics Institute will present “AI-Enabled Multi-omic Cell-Free DNA Profiling for Multi-Cancer Detection: Technology Principles, Large Validation Datasets, and Pathways to Global Implementation.” The presentation will explore the scientific principles behind AI-enabled multi-omic cell-free DNA analysis and discuss the importance of large validation datasets in developing clinically relevant multi-cancer detection approaches. It will also examine considerations for broader implementation. Learning from Asian real-world evidence at scale Prof. Herbert Ho Fung Loong of the Chinese University of Hong Kong will present “Multi-Omic Liquid Biopsy Approaches in Precision Oncology: Asian Real-World Evidence at Scale, Affordability, and High-Precision Applications.” The session will discuss the value of dual tissue and liquid multi-omic profiling, with integrated hybrid tumour-informed and tumour-naïve ctDNA monitoring in early-stage and metastatic disease. Asian real-world evidence at scale will be presented, including considerations related to access and affordability. Exploring multi-omic signals and immunogenetic discovery Prof. Aya El-Helali of the University of Hong Kong will discuss “The Role of Multi-Omic Signals for Next-Generation Precision Oncology and Immunogenetic Discovery.” The presentation will explore how the integration of complementary biological signals—including genomic, transcriptomic, neoantigen, and tumour-microenvironment data—may address the limits of single-biomarker testing and support immunogenetic discovery . Connecting patient-derived models with precision medicine Dr. Vien Le of the Medical Genetics Institute will present “3D Patient-Derived Organoids in Precision Medicine: From Bench to Bedside.” The presentation will examine how patient-derived organoid models can add functional biological insight s and support the translation of laboratory innovation into precision medicine applications, including an ongoing clinical validation study. Within the broader symposium, this work will connect molecular profiling with a complementary model for better understanding individual tumor biology and advancing personalized cancer care. From regional evidence to global precision oncology The programme will conclude with a panel discussion titled: “Bridging Regional Evidence to Global Precision Oncology: Challenges and Opportunities in Multi-omic Liquid Biopsy Implementation Across the Cancer Care Continuum.” Panelists will include: Prof. Herbert Ho Fung Loong, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR Prof. Umberto Malapelle, University Federico II of Naples, Italy Dr. Le Son Tran, Medical Genetics Institute, Viet Nam Prof. Aya El-Helali, The University of Hong Kong Dr. Vien Le, Medical Genetics Institute, Viet Nam Asst. Prof. Lucksamon Thamlikitkul, Siriraj Hospital, Mahidol University, Thailand The discussion will consider the practical and scientific requirements for translating regional evidence into broader clinical implementation, including evidence generation, affordability, healthcare infrastructure, clinical adoption, and the responsible deployment of new technologies. Asst. Prof. Thamlikitkul will also present a case study on hybrid ctDNA MRD monitoring in lung cancer from Thailand. A precision cell-free DNA platform across the cancer continuum Gene Solutions offers an integrated precision cell-free DNA platform for multi-omic screening, profiling and ctDNA monitoring across the cancer care continuum, with complementary functional models in development. The symposium reflects the company’s mission to make precision testing accessible to millions of people, so more patients can receive an answer in time to act. Symposium details Date: Friday, 23 October 2026 Time: 09:45–11:15 CEST Venue: Salamanca Auditorium, Hall 10 Location: IFEMA Madrid, Spain Official session page: https://cslide.ctimeetingtech.com/esmo2026/attendee/confcal/show/session/106 This non-promotional medical educational symposium is organized and funded by Gene Solutions for healthcare professionals only. # FragMIL: A Fragment-Token Multiple-Instance Learning Framework for Cancer Detection from Cell-Free DNA Fragmentomics

More formats

[Order Reprints](https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6694/18/20/3389/reprints)

## Simple Summary

Blood contains small pieces of DNA released from cells throughout the body, including cancer cells. How these DNA pieces are cut—their length, the sequence at their ends, and where they come from in the genome—differs between people with and without cancer and can be measured with low-cost, low-coverage whole-genome sequencing. Existing tests usually condense millions of DNA pieces into a small set of average measurements, which may lose useful information. We developed FragMIL, an artificial intelligence approach that learns directly from thousands of individual DNA pieces per person and combines them into a single cancer score. Using public data from 934 individuals in three studies covering multiple cancer types, lung cancer, and liver cancer, FragMIL detected cancer more accurately than four established methods and remained informative across cancer stages and types. With prospective clinical validation, this approach could help improve blood-based cancer detection.

## Abstract

**Background/Objectives**: Cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics from low-coverage whole-genome sequencing (lcWGS) is a promising approach for non-invasive cancer detection. However, most existing methods summarize millions of cfDNA fragments into handcrafted sample-level features before classification, potentially discarding informative patterns carried by individual molecules. We aimed to develop and benchmark a framework that learns directly from fragment-level signals. **Methods**: We developed FragMIL, a fragment-token multiple-instance learning framework that represents each cfDNA molecule as a learnable token integrating end-motif, genomic-position, and fragment-length information, and aggregates thousands of fragment tokens into a patient-level cancer score. FragMIL was evaluated on 934 samples from three public lcWGS cohorts (pan-cancer, lung cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma) using five repeated subject-level splits, a 288-configuration design-space benchmark, and comparison with four established fragmentomic approaches (coverage, DELFI, end motif, and fragment size). **Results**: FragMIL achieved the highest mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) in every cohort, with 0.963 ± 0.009, 0.802 ± 0.009, and 0.910 ± 0.015 in the DELFI/Cristiano 2019, LUCAS/Mathios 2021, and Jiang 2015 cohorts, respectively. End-motif encoding provided the strongest standalone discriminative signal, whereas the optimal fragment pool was cohort-dependent, with open chromatin region fragments performing best for pan-cancer detection and tumor-enriched fragments for disease-specific cohorts. Performance was retained across cancer stages and cancer types. **Conclusions**: Preserving molecule-level fragmentomic information improves cancer detection, supporting fragment-token learning as a promising framework for next-generation cfDNA fragmentomics.

## ABSTRACT

### Background

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) lacks an established screening program, and most cases are diagnosed at advanced stages. Multi-cancer early detection (MCED) blood-based assays represent a promising approach, yet real-world clinical experience with MCED-identified HNSCC remains limited.

### Methods

We retrospectively reviewed patients referred to our Otolaryngology department with a positive Galleri MCED result indicating HNSCC between January 2020 and March 2026. Physical exam findings, flexible laryngoscopy findings, imaging, and treatment data for each patient was reviewed.

### Results

Three patients were included in this case report. All three patients were diagnosed with early-stage p16+ oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma despite absent symptoms and largely unremarkable physical examinations. All underwent successful resection with no evidence of recurrent disease at early follow-up.

### Conclusions

MCED testing can potentially identify early-stage HNSCC in asymptomatic patients. Otolaryngologists should be prepared to systematically evaluate patients referred following a positive MCED result.

## 1 Introduction

Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) represents a growing global health burden without an established population-level screening program. Survival is highly stage-dependent, with 5-year rates ranging from 70%–90% for early-stage disease to 25%–60% for locoregionally advanced disease and less than 20% for metastatic disease \[[1](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hed.70337#hed70337-bib-0001)\]. This stark survival gradient underscores the critical importance of early detection.

Development of screening tools for HNSCC is challenging for several reasons. The low prevalence of HNSCC in the general population, heterogeneous disease states across multiple anatomic sites, and the absence of a single accessible target organ or precursor lesion all complicate screening program design. The anatomic inaccessibility of common HNSCC primary sites to routine physical examination also poses a significant barrier to early detection. Tumors arising in the nasopharynx, base of tongue, supraglottic larynx, and hypopharynx often remain undetected without specialized fiberoptic examination, resulting in late-stage presentation and poor clinical outcomes \[[2](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hed.70337#hed70337-bib-0002)\].

This diagnostic gap has driven interest in novel, minimally invasive approaches to cancer detection. Liquid biopsy strategies, which analyze tumor derived material circulating in the bloodstream, have emerged as a promising avenue for early detection for malignancy. In HPV-positive oropharyngeal cancer specifically, commercially available circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) tests such as NavDx (Naveris, Waltham, MA, USA) have demonstrated clinical utility for surveillance purposes and are especially beneficial for screening in high-risk populations \[[3](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hed.70337#hed70337-bib-0003)\]. However, new tests on the horizon purport to move beyond single-cancer identification, screening for many cancer types in a single assay. These so-called multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests are blood-based assays that analyze circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA). One such MCED test, Galleri (GRAIL, Menlo Park, CA, USA), has garnered attention for its potential to screen across a wide range of cancer types by leveraging circulating DNA methylation patterns \[[4](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hed.70337#hed70337-bib-0004)\]. Early institutional experience at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute demonstrated that among 14 patients presenting with a positive Galleri result, 78.6% had a confirmed cancer diagnosis \[[5](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/hed.70337#hed70337-bib-0005)\]. _Veteran biotech CFO and former healthcare investment banker joins the DELFI board as the company advances FirstLook Lung toward a pivotal data readout and FDA submission_

PALO ALTO, Calif., April 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ - **\-** [**DELFI Diagnostics, Inc.**](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4673428-1&h=2947400382&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdelfidiagnostics.com%2F&a=DELFI+Diagnostics%2C+Inc.) **,** developer of innovative AI-powered blood-based tests that leverage cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics for cancer detection and monitoring, today announced the appointment of Charles "Charlie" Newton to its Board of Directors. Mr. Newton brings nearly three decades of healthcare finance and executive leadership experience to DELFI as the company reads out pivotal data that advances its lead product, FirstLook™ Lung, toward FDA submission and positions it for broad commercial adoption.

"Charlie's deep financial expertise combined with his experience with emerging companies gives him a unique and valuable perspective. We are thrilled he has chosen to join us in our mission to deliver a paradigm-changing screening test for lung cancer," said Liz Homans, Chair of the DELFI Diagnostics Board of Directors.

"Charlie's addition to our Board reflects where DELFI is today — we are on the cusp of unblinding pivotal clinical data, and we have an FDA submission on the horizon. We welcome Charlie to the Board and our mission to change the future of lung cancer screening. I look forward to his counsel as we evaluate transformative partnerships that could accelerate our growth and clinical impact," said Susan Tousi, Chief Executive Officer of DELFI Diagnostics.

"DELFI is tackling one of the most important unmet needs in oncology, and the combination of a differentiated fragmentomics platform, an integrated AI approach, a clear path to FDA approval and broad reimbursement makes this an exciting time to join the Board," said Mr. Newton.

Mr. Newton most recently served as Chief Financial Officer of Lyell Immunopharma, where he led the company's initial public offering, one of the largest biotech IPOs in NASDAQ history, and oversaw finance, corporate development, investor relations, and corporate strategy. Prior to Lyell, he spent more than 25 years in healthcare investment banking, including senior leadership roles as Managing Director and Co-Head of Healthcare Investment Banking in the Americas at Bank of America Merrill Lynch and Credit Suisse, and as Managing Director and Head of Western Region Healthcare Investment Banking at Morgan Stanley. Across his investment banking career, he advised on approximately $200 billion in mergers and acquisitions and helped clients raise nearly $60 billion in capital.

Mr. Newton currently serves on the boards of directors of Novavax, Inc., Coherus Oncology, Inc., and Keros Therapeutics, Inc. He previously served on the boards of 2seventy bio, Inc. until its acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb, and Carmot Therapeutics until its acquisition by Roche. Mr. Newton holds an M.B.A. from The Tuck School of Business at Dartmouth College and a B.S. in Finance from Miami University.

**About DELFI Diagnostics**

DELFI Diagnostics is developing next-generation, blood-based tests that are convenient, accessible, and reliable, offering a new way to help detect cancer. DELFI's proprietary technology leverages advanced AI to analyze patterns of circulating cell-free DNA fragments in the blood, an approach known as fragmentomics, to help detect lung cancer with high sensitivity. FirstLook Lung, the first commercially available blood-based screening test for lung cancer in the United States, serves individuals eligible for lung cancer screening through a simple blood draw that integrates with routine blood work. With a negative predictive value of 99.8 percent, the test identifies individuals at elevated risk for lung cancer, including early-stage disease, and guides them toward follow-up with guideline-recommended low-dose CT. Through novel health system partnerships, DELFI is pioneering electronic medical record (EMR) integration that makes blood-based testing available to historically underserved populations. FirstLook Lung has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

DELFI-Tumor Fraction (DELFI-TF) is a liquid biopsy research service for monitoring late-stage cancer patients during their course of treatment. As a versatile precision medicine platform, DELFI-TF provides a non-invasive, tissue-free, and tumor-agnostic quantitative estimate of tumor burden at the time of the blood draw. Based on the standard DELFI cfDNA assay, DELFI-TF overcomes many of the barriers of currently available monitoring products, such as cost, turnaround time, sensitivity, and tissue biopsy, while maintaining market-level performance. DELFI-TF provides critical therapeutic monitoring insights across all solid cancer and treatment types by establishing molecular profiles, tracking therapeutic effectiveness, and identifying emerging resistance patterns earlier than traditional methods. DELFI-TF has not been cleared or approved by the FDA and is intended for research use only.

To learn more about DELFI Diagnostics, visit [DELFIDiagnostics.com](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4673428-1&h=1697985973&u=http%3A%2F%2Fdelfidiagnostics.com%2F&a=DELFIDiagnostics.com)

[Accessibility Statement](https://www.cision.com/about/accessibility/) [Skip Navigation](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/delfi-diagnostics-to-showcase-whole-genome-cfdna-platform-advances-in-cancer-detection-and-monitoring-at-aacr-2026-annual-meeting-302734115.html?tc=eml_cleartime#main)

_Five poster presentations span lung cancer early detection, immunotherapy response prediction, cancer subtyping, treatment monitoring, and next-generation sequencing platforms_

PALO ALTO, Calif., April 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- [**DELFI Diagnostics, Inc.**](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4657274-1&h=752600638&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdelfidiagnostics.com%2F&a=DELFI+Diagnostics%2C+Inc.), developer of innovative blood-based tests that leverage whole-genome cell-free DNA (cfDNA)  assays for cancer detection and monitoring, today announced it will present five poster presentations at the [**American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) 2026 Annual Meeting**](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4657274-1&h=2256521199&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.aacr.org%2Fmeeting%2Faacr-annual-meeting-2026%2F&a=American+Association+for+Cancer+Research+(AACR)+2026+Annual+Meeting), taking place April 17–22, 2026 in San Diego, CA. The presentations highlight advances across DELFI's platform, including lung cancer subtyping, immunotherapy response prediction, the clinical utility of ctDNA-based molecular response, treatment monitoring on ultra high-throughput, next-generation sequencing platforms, and colorectal cancer treatment response monitoring.

"This year's AACR presentations reflect the breadth and maturity of our AI-driven, computational platform," said Susan Tousi, CEO. "From early detection to treatment monitoring, we're generating clinical evidence across the cancer continuum that reinforces the power of genome-wide cfDNA analysis combined with AI. These five abstracts represent meaningful contributions from our team and our academic collaborators at Johns Hopkins and the Netherlands Cancer Institute."

**Poster Presentations at AACR 2026**

Sunday, April 19 \| 2:00–5:00 PM PT

**Cell-Free DNA Fragmentome Profiles Predict Immunotherapy Response**

- Session: Liquid Biopsies: Circulating Nucleic Acids 1
- Poster Section 44, Board 15 \| Abstract #1134
- Presenter: Valsamo Anagnostou, MD, PhD, Johns Hopkins University

**Lung Cancer Subtyping Using Cell-Free DNA Fragmentomes and Protein Biomarkers**

- Session: Liquid Biopsies: Circulating Nucleic Acids 1
- Poster Section 44, Board 16 \| Abstract #1135
- Presenter: Laurel Millberg, MSc, DELFI Diagnostics

**Clinical Utility of Landmark ctDNA Molecular Response as an Early Indicator of Immunotherapy Outcomes in Lung Cancer**

- Session: Liquid Biopsy: Multi-Analyte and Multi-Omic
- Poster Section 5, Board 17 \| Abstract #110
- Presenter: Jaime Wehr, MS, Johns Hopkins University

Monday, April 20 \| 2:00–5:00 PM PT

**Enhanced cfDNA Fragmentation-Based Treatment Monitoring on the Ultima Genomics Platform**

- Session: Liquid Biopsies: Circulating Nucleic Acids 3
- Poster Section 45, Board 24 \| Abstract #3863
- Presenter: Laurel Millberg, MSc, DELFI Diagnostics

Tuesday, April 21 \| 9:00 AM–12:00 PM PT

**Cell-Free DNA Fragmentomes for Treatment Response Monitoring in Patients with Metastatic Colorectal Cancer: The DOLPHIN Study**

- Session: Liquid Biopsies: Circulating Nucleic Acids 4
- Poster Section 45, Board 20 \| Abstract #5325
- Presenter: Denise van Steijn, MSc, Netherlands Cancer Institute

The five presentations reflect the expanding clinical evidence base for DELFI's technology platform, which uses AI and machine learning to analyze genome-wide patterns of cell-free DNA fragmentation in blood. The research spans early detection, cancer subtyping, immunotherapy response prediction, and treatment monitoring across multiple cancer types and sequencing platforms.

In early detection, DELFI has clinically validated FirstLook Lung, a blood-based test designed to improve early detection of lung cancer, the leading cause of cancer death in the United States. New data being presented at AACR 2026 extend the platform's capabilities into lung cancer subtyping and immunotherapy response prediction, demonstrating how fragmentation patterns and protein biomarkers can provide clinical insights beyond initial detection.

On the treatment-monitoring front, DELFI-TF\*, the company's tumor-fraction-based monitoring solution, continues to generate clinical validation data across cancer types. The DOLPHIN study presentation describes a multicenter, prospective, observational study from the Netherlands Cancer Institute that examines new potential applications for cfDNA-based treatment response monitoring in ~500 colorectal cancer patients treated with systemic chemotherapy.

Additionally, new DELFI-TF data generated on the Ultima Genomics platform underscore the adaptability of DELFI's core genomics technology and identify promising avenues for performance enhancement in future product generations.

"We are excited to present our latest work in early detection, treatment monitoring, subtyping, and technology innovation, " said Amoolya Singh, PhD, Chief Technology Officer. "We continue to believe that the sensitivity, low cost, and versatility of our technical approach position us well for continued scientific discovery and product development."

Attendees are invited to visit DELFI Diagnostics at **Booth #1711** or request a meeting at **[https://about.delfidiagnostics.com/aacr2026/](https://about.delfidiagnostics.com/aacr2026/)**. For more information about DELFI's fragmentomics platform, visit **[www.delfidiagnostics.com](http://www.delfidiagnostics.com/)**.

_\*The DELFI-TF Assay and related services are for Research Purposes Only and are not intended for diagnostic procedures or applications._

**About DELFI Diagnostics**

DELFI Diagnostics is developing next-generation, blood-based tests that are convenient, accessible, and reliable, offering a new way to help detect cancer. DELFI's proprietary technology leverages advanced AI to analyze patterns of circulating cell-free DNA fragments in the blood, an approach known as fragmentomics, to help detect lung cancer with high sensitivity. FirstLook Lung, the first commercially available blood-based screening test for lung cancer in the United States, serves individuals eligible for lung cancer screening through a simple blood draw that integrates with routine blood work. With a negative predictive value of 99.8 percent, the test identifies individuals at elevated risk for lung cancer, including early-stage disease, and guides them toward follow-up with guideline-recommended low-dose CT. Through novel health system partnerships, DELFI is pioneering electronic medical record (EMR) integration that makes blood-based testing available to historically underserved populations. FirstLook Lung has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

DELFI-Tumor Fraction (DELFI-TF) is a liquid biopsy research service for monitoring late-stage cancer patients during their course of treatment. As a versatile precision medicine platform, DELFI-TF provides a non-invasive, tissue-free, and tumor-agnostic quantitative estimate of tumor burden at the time of the blood draw. Based on the standard DELFI cfDNA assay, DELFI-TF overcomes many of the barriers of currently available monitoring products such as cost, turnaround time, sensitivity, and tissue biopsy, while maintaining market-level performance. DELFI-TF provides critical therapeutic monitoring insights across all solid cancer and treatment types by establishing molecular profiles, tracking therapeutic effectiveness, and identifying emerging resistance patterns earlier than traditional methods. DELFI-TF has not been cleared or approved by the FDA and is intended for research use only.

items.title: DELFI Diagnostics Appoints Cindy Soriano as Chief Financial Officer and Announces Participation in 44th Annual J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference
items.content:
[Accessibility Statement](https://www.cision.com/about/accessibility/) [Skip Navigation](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/delfi-diagnostics-appoints-cindy-soriano-as-chief-financial-officer-and-announces-participation-in-44th-annual-jp-morgan-healthcare-conference-302655846.html?tc=eml_cleartime#main)

_Experienced finance leader to guide company through critical clinical and regulatory milestones; CEO to present at premier healthcare investment event_

PALO ALTO, Calif., Jan. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- [DELFI Diagnostics, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4591618-1&h=2646265135&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdelfidiagnostics.com%2F&a=DELFI+Diagnostics%2C+Inc.), developer of accessible blood-based, liquid biopsy tests that deliver a new way to enhance early cancer detection, today announced the appointment of Cindy Soriano as Chief Financial Officer, effective immediately. The company also announced that Chief Executive Officer, Susan Tousi, will present at the 44th Annual [J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4591618-1&h=1078361225&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.jpmorgan.com%2Fabout-us%2Fevents-conferences%2Fhealth-care-conference&a=J.P.+Morgan+Healthcare+Conference) in San Francisco.

"Cindy's promotion comes at a pivotal moment for DELFI as we prepare to achieve key clinical and regulatory milestones," said Susan Tousi. "Over the past three and a half years as Vice President of Finance and Investor Relations, Cindy has been instrumental in building our financial foundation and guiding us through two successful fundraising rounds. Her strategic vision, operational rigor, and collaborative approach will be essential as we work to deliver on our mission and create long-term value."

Cindy brings 20 years of finance leadership to the role. Prior to joining DELFI, Cindy held senior finance leadership roles across the life sciences sector, including leading the finance organization at Zogenix through its acquisition by UCB and post-transaction integration. Earlier, she held various leadership roles at BioMarin Pharmaceuticals supporting operational and strategic planning across a diverse portfolio of assets spanning pre-clinical, clinical, and commercial stages.

**J.P. Morgan Healthcare Conference Presentation** Susan Tousi, CEO, is scheduled to present on Thursday, January 15, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. PT at the Westin St. Francis hotel in San Francisco. The presentation will provide an update on DELFI's progress and strategic priorities.

**About DELFI Diagnostics** DELFI Diagnostics is developing next-generation, blood-based tests that are accurate, accessible, and deliver a new way to help detect cancer. DELFI tests are built to solve the highest-burden population health issues, including in historically underserved demographics, and have the potential to save lives on a global scale. FirstLook Lung, for individuals eligible for lung cancer screening, is our first laboratory-developed screening test and requires a simple blood draw that can be incorporated with routine blood work. The test is based on fragmentomics, the discovery that cancer cells are more chaotic than normal cells and, when they die, leave behind tell-tale patterns and characteristics of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragments in the blood. The DELFI platform applies advanced machine-learning technology to whole-genome sequencing data to assess individuals' cfDNA fragments against populations with and without cancer. FirstLook Lung uses these millions of data points to reliably identify individuals who may have cancer detected through low-dose CT, including early-stage disease, with a negative predictive value of 99.8 percent. This test has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. To learn more about DELFI Diagnostics, visit DELFIDiagnostics.com.

This inclusion validates our strategic choice to list on the HKEX and reinforces our commitment to expanding our global investor footprint. The HSCI, which serves as a key benchmark for the Hong Kong stock market, covers around the top 95% of the total market capitalisation of companies listed on the Main Board. To get on the HSCI, a company must meet a strict set of criteria focused on its size, trading activity, and representation within the broader Hong Kong market. items.title: DELFI Diagnostics to Present Early Detection and Advanced Cancer Monitoring Technology Updates at AACR Annual Meeting
items.content:
[Accessibility Statement](https://www.cision.com/about/accessibility/) [Skip Navigation](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/delfi-diagnostics-to-present-early-detection-and-advanced-cancer-monitoring-technology-updates-at-aacr-annual-meeting-302433845.html#main)

_Fragmentomics pioneer showcases DELFI-TF treatment monitoring solution alongside early detection capabilities at a premier oncology research event_

BALTIMORE and PALO ALTO, Calif., April 25, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- [DELFI Diagnostics, Inc](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4409727-1&h=379526652&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdelfidiagnostics.com%2F&a=DELFI+Diagnostics%2C+Inc) **.**, developer of innovative blood-based tests that leverage cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragmentomics for cancer detection and monitoring, today announced its team is presenting at the upcoming [2025 American Association for Cancer Research (AACR)](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4409727-1&h=415277104&u=https%3A%2F%2Fabout.delfidiagnostics.com%2Faacr2025%2F&a=2025+American+Association+for+Cancer+Research+(AACR)+)Annual Meeting in Chicago, IL. DELFI is showcasing its groundbreaking DELFI-TF technology for treatment response monitoring alongside its early detection capabilities.

"Our presentations at AACR highlight how DELFI's fragmentomics platform is transforming both early cancer detection and treatment monitoring," said Victor E. Velculescu, MD, PhD, DELFI Diagnostics Founder and Board Director. "The DELFI technology represents a paradigm shift in how we detect cancer by combining genome-wide fragmentomics of DNA in the blood with AI algorithms for high sensitivity in the screening setting as well as for noninvasively measuring treatment efficacy in advanced cancer patients. "

DELFI is presenting multiple podium and poster sessions at AACR, including:

**Genomic and fragmentomic landscapes of cell-free DNA for early cancer detection** presented by Victor E. Velculescu, MD, PhD

- Tuesday, April 29, 11:06 AM - 11:26 AM CT
- Room S100 BC (Grand Ballroom BC) - McCormick Place South

**Leveraging the cfDNA fragmentome to predict immunotherapy response** presented by Valsamo Anagnostou, MD, PhD

- Monday, April 28, 3:05 PM - 3:20 PM CT
- Room S105 - McCormick Place South

**Analysis of lung cancer clinical characteristics using cell-free DNA fragmentomes** presented by Lorenzo Rinaldi, PhD

- Monday, April 28, 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM CT
- Section 28, Poster 29

**Cell-free DNA fragmentomes for treatment response monitoring in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer: the DOLPHIN study** presented by Denise E. Van Steijn

- Monday, April 28, 2:00 PM - 5:00 PM CT
- Section 29, Poster 6

DELFI Diagnostics has clinically validated FirstLook Lung, its blood test designed to improve early detection of lung cancer, which remains the leading cause of cancer deaths in the United States. At the AACR Annual Meeting, DELFI will present research data on early detection in additional cancer types, including liver, ovarian, and other cancers.

In addition to the company's early detection efforts, DELFI launched the DELFI-TF\* research service in February 2024. DELFI-TF actively guides critical oncology drug development decisions at five top 20 pharmaceutical companies. The technology is designed to deliver critical insights at every stage of the metastatic cancer journey, from baseline assessment and response monitoring to resistance detection and continuous insight across all treatment lines. Requiring just 800µl of plasma, DELFI-TF offers a mutation-independent monitoring solution with a 99% success rate and results typically available in 10-14 business days.

DELFI-TF's performance has been validated through clinical studies across multiple cancers, including colorectal, lung, pancreatic, breast, melanoma, and head and neck. It has demonstrated its ability to quantify tumor burden without requiring mutation profiling. This strongly correlates with Mutant Allele Frequency (MAF) measurements even when specific mutations are undetectable.

"Lack of efficacy is still the most common reason for Oncology Phase II clinical trials to fail during development, demonstrating the need for improved methods for detection of efficacy of new medical entities in early clinical trials," said Nicholas C. Dracopoli, PhD, Chief Scientific Officer and Co-Founder. "DELFI-TF offers pharmaceutical developers a streamlined, cost-effective solution for monitoring treatment response earlier and more efficiently than traditional methods."

To learn more about DELFI Diagnostics and its innovative fragmentomics platform, visit them at **AACR Booth #2060** or visit **[www.delfidiagnostics.com](https://c212.net/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4409727-1&h=3865836998&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.delfidiagnostics.com%2F&a=www.delfidiagnostics.com)**.

\*The DELFI-TF Assay and related services are for Research Purposes Only and are not intended for diagnostic procedures or applications.

**About DELFI Diagnostics** DELFI Diagnostics is developing next-generation, blood-based tests that are accurate, accessible, and deliver a new way to help detect cancer. DELFI tests are built to solve the highest-burden population health issues, including in historically underserved demographics, and have the potential to save lives on a global scale. FirstLook Lung, for individuals eligible for lung cancer screening, is our first laboratory-developed screening test and requires a simple blood draw that can be incorporated with routine blood work. The test is based on fragmentomics, the discovery that cancer cells are more chaotic than normal cells and, when they die, leave behind tell-tale patterns and characteristics of cell-free DNA (cfDNA) fragments in the blood. The DELFI platform applies advanced machine-learning technology to whole-genome sequencing data to assess individuals' cfDNA fragments against populations with and without cancer. FirstLook Lung uses these millions of data points to reliably identify individuals who may have cancer detected through low-dose CT, including early-stage disease, with a negative predictive value of 99.8 percent. This test has not been cleared or approved by the FDA.

## Guardant Health Prices $500 Million Convertible Senior Notes Offering

November 12, 2026

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--  Guardant Health, Inc. (“Guardant Health”) (Nasdaq: GH), a leading precision oncology company, today announced the pricing of its offering of $500 million aggregate principal amount of 0% convertible senior notes due 2032 (the “notes”) in a private offering (the “offering”) to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). The issuance and sale of the notes are scheduled to settle on November 16, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Guardant Health also granted the initial purchasers of the notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the notes are first issued, up to an additional $50.0 million aggregate principal amount of notes.

The notes will be senior, unsecured obligations of Guardant Health. The notes will not bear regular interest, and the principal amount of the notes will not accrete. The notes will mature on May 15, 2032, unless earlier converted, redeemed or repurchased by Guardant Health. Before February 15, 2032, noteholders will have the right to convert all or any portion of their notes only in certain circumstances. From and after February 15, 2032 until the close of business on the second scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, noteholders may convert their notes at any time at their election. Guardant Health will settle conversions by paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its common stock or a combination of cash and shares of its common stock, at Guardant Health’s election. The initial conversion rate is 4.7858 shares of common stock per $1,000 principal amount of notes, which represents an initial conversion price of approximately $208.95 per share of common stock, and will be subject to customary anti-dilution adjustments. The initial conversion price represents a premium of approximately 35.0% above the last reported sale price of $154.78 per share of Guardant Health’s common stock on November 11, 2026.

Except as described in the second succeeding sentence with respect to a cleanup redemption, the notes will not be redeemable at Guardant Health’s election at any time before November 20, 2029. The redemption price for any provisional redemption or cleanup redemption, as applicable, will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be redeemed, plus accrued and unpaid special interest and additional interest, if any, to, but excluding, the redemption date.

If a “fundamental change” (as defined in the indenture for the notes) occurs, then, subject to limited exceptions, noteholders may require Guardant Health to repurchase their notes for cash. The repurchase price will be equal to the principal amount of the notes to be repurchased, plus accrued and unpaid special interest and additional interest, if any, to, but excluding, the applicable fundamental change repurchase date. In addition, following certain corporate events that occur prior to the maturity date of the notes or if Guardant Health delivers a notice of redemption, Guardant Health will, in certain circumstances, increase the conversion rate of the notes for a noteholder who elects to convert its notes in connection with such a corporate event or convert its notes called (or deemed called) for redemption during the related redemption period, as the case may be.

## Guardant Health Announces Proposed $500.0 Million Offering of Convertible Senior Notes Due 2032

November 11, 2026

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
Guardant Health, Inc. (“Guardant Health”) (Nasdaq: GH), a leading precision oncology company, today announced its intention to offer $500.0 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes due 2032 (the “notes”) in a private offering (the “offering”) to persons reasonably believed to be qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”). Guardant Health also intends to grant the initial purchasers of the notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the notes are first issued, up to an additional $50.0 million aggregate principal amount of notes. The offering is subject to market and other conditions, and there can be no assurance as to whether or when the offering may be completed, or as to the actual size or terms of the offering.

The notes will be senior, unsecured obligations of Guardant Health, will accrue interest payable semi-annually in arrears and will mature on May 15, 2032, unless earlier converted, redeemed or repurchased by Guardant Health. Noteholders will have the right to convert all or any portion of their notes in certain circumstances and during specified periods. Guardant Health will settle conversions by paying or delivering, as applicable, cash, shares of its common stock or a combination of cash and shares of its common stock, at Guardant Health’s election.

Except as described in the second succeeding sentence with respect to a cleanup redemption, the notes will not be redeemable at Guardant Health’s election at any time before November 20, 2029. The notes will be redeemable, in whole or in part, for cash at Guardant Health’s option at any time, and from time to time, on a redemption date on or after November 20, 2029 and on or before the 25th scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date, but only if the last reported sale price per share of Guardant Health’s common stock exceeds 130% of the conversion price for a specified period of time. In addition, Guardant Health may redeem for cash all, but not less than all, of the notes at any time on or before the 25th scheduled trading day immediately before the maturity date if the aggregate principal amount of the notes outstanding at the time Guardant Health sends the related redemption notice is less than $50.0 million and the notes are freely tradable as of the date Guardant Health sends the related redemption notice. The interest rate, initial conversion rate and other terms of the notes will be determined at the pricing of the offering.

Guardant Health expects to use a portion of the net proceeds to repurchase for cash a portion of its 0% convertible senior notes due 2027 (the “2027 notes”) in the note repurchase transactions described below. In addition, Guardant Health intends to use a portion of the net proceeds to fund the cost of entering into the capped call transactions described below. Guardant Health intends to use the remainder of the net proceeds, if any, for general corporate purposes. General corporate purposes may include the acquisition of complementary products, technologies, intellectual property or businesses as part of Guardant Health’s growth strategy; however, Guardant Health currently does not have any agreements or commitments to complete any such transactions. If the initial purchasers exercise their option to purchase additional notes, then Guardant Health intends to use a portion of the additional net proceeds from the sale of the additional notes to fund the cost of entering into additional capped call transactions as described below. This press release is not an offer to repurchase any 2027 notes and the offering is not contingent upon the repurchase of any 2027 notes. There can be no assurances that Guardant Health will repurchase any 2027 notes.

In connection with the pricing of the notes, Guardant Health intends to enter into privately negotiated capped call transactions with one or more of the initial purchasers and/or their respective affiliates and/or other financial institutions (the “option counterparties”). The capped call transactions will cover, subject to customary adjustments, the number of shares of common stock initially underlying the notes. The capped call transactions are expected generally to reduce potential dilution to Guardant Health’s common stock upon conversion of the notes or at Guardant Health’s election (subject to certain conditions) offset any cash payments Guardant Health is required to make in excess of the aggregate principal amount of converted notes, as the case may be, with such reduction or offset subject to a cap.

Guardant Health expects to use a portion of the net proceeds to repurchase for cash a portion of the 2027 notes in privately negotiated transactions (each, a “note repurchase transaction”) entered into concurrently with the pricing of the offering through one of the initial purchasers or its affiliate, as Guardant Health’s agent. The terms of each note repurchase transaction will depend on a variety of factors, including the market price of Guardant Health’s common stock and the trading price of the 2027 notes at the time of such note repurchase transactions. No assurance can be given as to how much, if any, of the 2027 notes will be repurchased or the terms on which they will be repurchased.

Guardant Health has been advised that, in connection with establishing their initial hedges of the capped call transactions, the option counterparties or their respective affiliates expect to purchase shares of Guardant Health’s common stock and/or enter into various derivative transactions with respect to Guardant Health’s common stock concurrently with or shortly after the pricing of the notes

## Kevin Sayer Joins Guardant Health Board of Directors

November 3, 2026

PALO ALTO, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--
Guardant Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: GH), a leading precision oncology company, today announced the appointment of Kevin Sayer to its board of directors. Mr. Sayer is former CEO of Dexcom, Inc. and current Executive Chairman of the Dexcom board, with decades of strategic leadership experience in digital health technology.

“We are excited to welcome Kevin Sayer to Guardant’s board,” said Helmy Eltoukhy, chairman and co-CEO of Guardant Health. “Kevin has played a pivotal role in advancing innovations that have transformed how people monitor and manage disease and has a strategic and operations record delivering significant growth. His expertise will be invaluable to Guardant as we continue to pioneer innovations in how we screen, monitor, and treat disease.”

“Guardant’s leadership in liquid biopsy puts it in a powerful position to shape the next era of cancer care and disease detection, where AI can turn increasingly rich molecular data into more precise, actionable insights,” said Mr. Sayer. “I’m excited to work with the team to build on that leadership and help bring the benefits of earlier detection and more personalized treatment to more patients.”

Mr. Sayer has served as Executive Chair of the Dexcom board since 2026, as Chairman of the Board since 2018, and as a director on the board since 2007. Additionally, Mr. Sayer served as CEO of Dexcom from 2015 to 2026, and as a Dexcom executive since 2011. Prior to his roles at Dexcom, Mr. Sayer served as CFO of Biosensors International Group, Ltd., as an independent healthcare and medical technology industry consultant, as EVP and CFO of Specialty Laboratories, Inc., and as CFO of MiniMed, Inc. Mr. Sayer is a Certified Public Accountant (inactive) and received his Master’s Degree in Accounting and Information Systems concurrently with a B.A., both from Brigham Young University.

**About Guardant Health**

Guardant Health is a leading precision oncology company focused on guarding wellness and giving every person more time free from cancer. Founded in 2012, Guardant is transforming patient care and accelerating new cancer therapies by providing critical insights into what drives disease through its advanced blood and tissue tests, real-world data and AI analytics. Guardant tests help improve outcomes across all stages of care, including screening to find cancer early, monitoring for recurrence in early-stage cancer, and treatment selection for patients with advanced cancer. For more information, visit [guardanthealth.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fguardanthealth.com%2F&esheet=54634628&newsitemid=20261103598275&lan=en-US&anchor=guardanthealth.com&index=1&md5=06c1b61a83376be4cf557618d23b3dc8) and follow the company on [LinkedIn](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fcompany%2Fguardanthealth&esheet=54634628&newsitemid=20261103598275&lan=en-US&anchor=LinkedIn&index=2&md5=ba7ea575e94aa52960a83f5b0abaa0a6), [X (Twitter)](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Ftwitter.com%2FGuardantHealth&esheet=54634628&newsitemid=20261103598275&lan=en-US&anchor=X+%28Twitter%29&index=3&md5=a15aa4acef4d1470c4cf365b08478158) and [Facebook](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2Fguardanthealth&esheet=54634628&newsitemid=20261103598275&lan=en-US&anchor=Facebook&index=4&md5=52c3c01739767f78e451ae3b75ae4ec7).

## Highlights

- •
Current cancer screening protocols systematically underserve low-income and minority populations.

- •
PRS, AI, MCED tests and life-course models risk reproducing existing inequities if poorly implemented.

- •
Ancestral bias in genomic and imaging datasets limits technology performance in diverse populations.

- •
NHS-Galleri trial shows MCED promise but highlights health system readiness as critical barrier.

- •
Equitable screening requires diverse data, public-system integration, and follow-up capacity.

## Abstract

Cancer screening programmes have substantially reduced cancer mortality in high-income settings, yet their benefits remain unequally distributed. Current protocols are largely based on trials conducted in predominantly white, middle-income populations, leaving significant gaps for minority, low-income, and high-risk groups. Four emerging technologies—polygenic risk scores (PRS), artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted imaging, multi-cancer early detection (MCED) tests, and life-course risk models—offer the possibility of moving beyond these limitations toward more individualised, risk-based screening. However, each technology also carries the risk of reproducing or amplifying existing inequities if the conditions under which it is developed and implemented are not carefully considered. PRS models are constrained by ancestral bias in genomic datasets; AI systems have been trained predominantly on data from high-income, low-diversity populations; MCED tests remain costly and largely inaccessible outside private healthcare; and life-course models depend on integrated longitudinal data infrastructures unavailable in most low- and middle-income settings. Evidence from the NHS-Galleri trial illustrates both the promise and complexity of translating novel screening technology into population-level benefit. This review argues that achieving equitable impact will require three interconnected changes: greater diversity in training data, earlier integration of new technologies into publicly funded health systems, and parallel investment in diagnostic and follow-up capacity. Without deliberate action across these dimensions, advances in cancer screening risk benefiting those already well served while leaving the most vulnerable populations further behind.

## Introduction

Cancer remains one of the leading causes of death worldwide. In 2022 alone, around 19.3 million new cases were diagnosed, and close to 10 million people lost their lives to the disease (Bray et al., 2024). Although early detection and treatment have improved survival rates in high-income countries, these improvements have not been experienced equally across the globe. There are still clear regional differences: for example, treatable cancer deaths account for only 7.6% of expected deaths in North America and 11.0% in Northern Europe, while the same figure rises to over 28–32% in sub-Saharan Africa (Langselius et al., 2026). These differences are not random. They reflect, at least in part, how screening systems are designed and implemented, as well as broader inequalities in access to timely diagnosis and effective care.

Organised cancer screening programmes are among the most effective tools available in modern oncology. Large randomised controlled trials (RCTs) have played a key role in shaping screening protocols for cancers such as breast, colorectal, cervical, and lung cancer in high-income settings. However, the populations included in these landmark trials—such as the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST), the Prostate, Lung, Colorectal and Ovarian Cancer Screening Trial (PLCO), and the Canadian National Breast Screening Study (NBSS)—were mostly middle-income individuals of European ancestry with stable access to healthcare (NLST Research Team, 2011, Gohagan et al., 2000, Miller et al., 2014). As Rothwell (2005) pointed out in a widely cited analysis, one of the main criticisms of RCTs is their limited external validity. In other words, these studies tend to work well for a “standard patient,” but real-world populations are far more diverse—and cancer does not limit itself to standard patients.

This mismatch has real consequences. There is increasing evidence that the stage at which cancer is diagnosed varies considerably with income level, ethnicity, and geographic location. People from low-income and minority backgrounds are more likely to be diagnosed at later stages (Loree et al., 2019). At the same time, colorectal cancer incidence in individuals under 50 has increased by about 51% over the past two decades, even though this group is largely excluded from current screening guidelines (Siegel et al., 2026).
